source.note: No real product. A generic Japandi visual proxy made for the demo catalogue; it copies no retailer's design and carries no brand.
source.generation: Higgsfield multi_image_to_3d from a four-view AI turnaround sheet generated with the Codex image_gen tool (codex-image.sh); should_texture=true, enable_pbr=true, should_remesh=true, topology=triangle, target_polycount=28000, symmetry_mode=auto, rigging and animation off.
source.postProcessing: @gltf-transform/cli resize --width 1024 --height 1024, then scripts/fit_glb.py per-axis fit (centres the footprint, puts the base at y=0), then emissiveFactor zeroed on the single material.
source.priceProvenance: invented: a plausible demo figure, not a real or quoted price

knownLimitations: No real product. Generic Japandi visual proxy generated from an AI turnaround sheet; the catalogue price is invented, not sourced.

Fit missed the listing box. Requested 65 x 12 x 170 cm, shipped 58.9 x 19.1 x 162.9 cm at the 10% anisotropy cap; fit_glb.py exited 1 with residuals -6.07 cm width, -7.08 cm height, +7.08 cm depth. The generated mirror is deeper than the listing's 12 cm because the reconstruction includes the rear support strut a free-standing leaning mirror needs. A uniform fit to 170 cm height instead would give about 61.5 x 21.9 x 170.0 cm with no distortion, if the coordinator prefers exact height over the listing footprint.

The frame HAS real depth: sampling vertices by height shows a dense slab cluster from z +4 to +10 cm (about 6 cm of solid timber) at every height band from 5 cm to 160 cm, with a separate rear strut cluster at z -6 to -2 cm and empty space between them. It is not a thin sheet.

The frame reconstructed UPRIGHT, not leaning. The slab cluster occupies the same z +4..+10 cm range at 5 cm height and at 160 cm height, so the reference sheet's ~8 degree backward lean was flattened out. It stands vertically on its own strut rather than raking back.
The mirror face is a flat matte pale panel by design, not a reflective surface: no reflection, no environment map. Prompting for a true reflection bakes garbage scenery into the texture.
Not inspected in a render; no render was available to this agent. All geometry claims above are read from vertex positions in the GLB.
PBR textures resized to 1024 px, so the oak grain is softer than the source sheet.
